questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Using the Bull’s Eye model, how many wall segments are used in the left ventricle?
questions.explanation: Per ASE, the LV is described with 16 or 17 segments — 16 for wall-motion scoring, and 17 when the apical cap is added (for perfusion/nuclear correlation). “16–17” captures both. *(Practice review slide 3.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Using the Bull’s Eye model, how many segments are used in the basal portion of the left ventricle?
questions.explanation: The basal region contains 6 segments: basal anterior, anteroseptal, inferoseptal, inferior, inferolateral, and anterolateral. *(Practice review slide 5.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Using the Bull’s Eye model, how many segments are used in the mid-cavity portion of the left ventricle?
questions.explanation: The mid-cavity region also has 6 segments, named analogously to the basal ring at the mid level. *(Practice review slide 7.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Using the Bull’s Eye model, how many segments are used in the apical portion of the left ventricle?
questions.explanation: The apical region has 4 segments: apical anterior, apical septal, apical inferior, and apical lateral. *(Practice review slide 9.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Where is the Moderator Band located?
options: Right atrium from IVC to interatrial septum
Left atrium from left atrial appendage to interatrial septum
questions.explanation: The moderator band lies in the RV apex, running from the interventricular septum to the anterior papillary muscle in the anterolateral RV free wall. *(Practice review slide 11.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What level of intercostal space is utilized in the apical window?
options: Near the point of maximal impulse in (the 5th intercostal space as starting point) the midaxillary line
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Near the point of maximal impulse in (the 5th intercostal space as starting point) the midaxillary line as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 13.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What walls are seen in the apical 4-chamber view?
questions.explanation: The apical 4-chamber profiles the inferoseptal (septal) wall and the anterolateral (lateral) wall of the LV. *(Practice review slide 15.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  In the Apical 4-Chamber view, the beam is directed towards the patient’s right shoulder. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: True — from the apex, the 4-chamber imaging plane is directed up toward the patient’s right shoulder, aligning the septum and lateral walls base-to-apex. *(Practice review slide 17.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  From Apical 4-Chamber, how do you maneuver the probe to acquire the 5-Chamber view?
questions.explanation: From the 4-chamber, angle the transducer anteriorly to bring up the LVOT, a segment of the aortic root, and the aortic valve — the apical 5-chamber. *(Practice review slide 19.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What apical view demonstrates the ‘floating disc’?
questions.explanation: In the apical 2-chamber view, the mitral valve appears as a “floating disc.” *(Practice review slide 21.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What walls are demonstrated in the 3-Chamber view?
questions.explanation: The apical 3-chamber (apical long-axis) displays the inferolateral (posterior) and anteroseptal walls. *(Practice review slide 23.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What walls are demonstrated in the 2-Chamber view?
questions.explanation: The apical 2-chamber demonstrates the inferior and anterior LV walls. *(Practice review slide 25.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  From Apical 4-Chamber, how do you maneuver the probe to acquire the 2-Chamber view?
questions.explanation: From the 4-chamber, rotate the transducer counterclockwise (indicator toward ~12–1 o’clock) to obtain the 2-chamber. *(Practice review slide 27.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What Apical view only demonstrates the left side of the heart?
questions.explanation: The apical 2-chamber shows only the left-sided chambers — the LV and LA. *(Practice review slide 29.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What Apical view demonstrates the Aortic valve?
questions.explanation: Both the apical 3-chamber and the apical 5-chamber demonstrate the aortic valve and LVOT. *(Practice review slide 31.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  The left-sided structures are more dominantly analyzed in echo compared to the right-sided structures. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: True — echo assessment is left-heart dominant, though right-sided structures and wall segments remain important. *(Practice review slide 33.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  The left side is harder to image compared to the right side. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: False — the right heart is generally the more challenging to image, given its anterior, retrosternal position and complex crescent geometry. *(Practice review slide 35.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  The apical window is located lateral and inferior on the chest wall. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: True — the apical window sits lateral and inferior on the chest wall, over the cardiac apex. *(Practice review slide 37.)*

questions.explanation: From the 4-chamber, angle the transducer anteriorly to bring up the LVOT, a segment of the aortic root, and the aortic valve — the apical 5-chamber. *(Practice review slide 19.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What apical view demonstrates the ‘floating disc’?
questions.explanation: In the apical 2-chamber view, the mitral valve appears as a “floating disc.” *(Practice review slide 21.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What walls are demonstrated in the 3-Chamber view?
questions.explanation: The apical 3-chamber (apical long-axis) displays the inferolateral (posterior) and anteroseptal walls. *(Practice review slide 23.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What walls are demonstrated in the 2-Chamber view?
questions.explanation: The apical 2-chamber demonstrates the inferior and anterior LV walls. *(Practice review slide 25.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  From Apical 4-Chamber, how do you maneuver the probe to acquire the 2-Chamber view?
questions.explanation: From the 4-chamber, rotate the transducer counterclockwise (indicator toward ~12–1 o’clock) to obtain the 2-chamber. *(Practice review slide 27.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What Apical view only demonstrates the left side of the heart?
questions.explanation: The apical 2-chamber shows only the left-sided chambers — the LV and LA. *(Practice review slide 29.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What Apical view demonstrates the Aortic valve?
questions.explanation: Both the apical 3-chamber and the apical 5-chamber demonstrate the aortic valve and LVOT. *(Practice review slide 31.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  The left-sided structures are more dominantly analyzed in echo compared to the right-sided structures. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: True — echo assessment is left-heart dominant, though right-sided structures and wall segments remain important. *(Practice review slide 33.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  The left side is harder to image compared to the right side. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: False — the right heart is generally the more challenging to image, given its anterior, retrosternal position and complex crescent geometry. *(Practice review slide 35.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  The apical window is located lateral and inferior on the chest wall. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: True — the apical window sits lateral and inferior on the chest wall, over the cardiac apex. *(Practice review slide 37.)*

questions.stem: A trainee is preparing for a practical echocardiography assessment.  Using the Bull’s Eye model, how many wall segments are used in the left ventricle?
questions.explanation: Per ASE, the LV is described with 16 or 17 segments — 16 for wall-motion scoring, and 17 when the apical cap is added (for perfusion/nuclear correlation). “16–17” captures both. *(Practice review slide 3.)*

questions.stem: A trainee is preparing for a practical echocardiography assessment.  Using the Bull’s Eye model, how many segments are used in the basal portion of the left ventricle?
questions.explanation: The basal region contains 6 segments: basal anterior, anteroseptal, inferoseptal, inferior, inferolateral, and anterolateral. *(Practice review slide 5.)*
